[RESPONSE] I don't recall having any episodes of fainting, near-fainting, or palpitations.

In a 60-year-old non-smoker with progressive exertional dyspnea and a normal echo, pulmonary vascular disease (including chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension), interstitial lung disease, occult COPD, anemia, or deconditioning remain possible. In a lifelong non-smoker, occupational or biomass exposures or alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency become likely causes. I need one specific exposure history before ordering targeted testing.

[QUERY] Have you ever been exposed long-term to indoor biomass smoke (wood, coal, dung) or worked in jobs with dusts/chemicals (mining, farming, construction, manufacturing, metalworking, or exposure to silica, asbestos, or welding fumes)? If yes, please specify the exposure and duration.

3. He has a 20-year history of working in the glass manufacturing industry
8. Long-term exposure to silica dust

Yes. I worked for 20 years in the glass manufacturing industry and had long-term exposure to silica dust.

[THOUGHT] A 60-year-old non-smoker with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnea, normal echocardiogram, spirometry showing fixed airflow obstruction (reduced FEV1/FVC without bronchodilator reversibility), normal lung volumes, and markedly reduced DLCO points to emphysematous COPD (loss of gas-exchanging surface) rather than restrictive or cardiac causes. Long-term occupational silica exposure (20 years in glass manufacturing) is a known cause of occupational emphysema/COPD in non-smokers. These findings make occupationally related emphysema (silica-induced COPD) the most likely diagnosis.

[DIAGNOSIS] Occupationally related emphysema (silica-induced COPD).
